transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-29
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); David Ortiz (Redwood SE); Ravi Patel (Redwood Product); Karla Singh (AurigaMesh Head of Integrations); Owen Park (AurigaMesh Platform Eng); Lena Fritz (AurigaMesh PM)
Shared artifacts: slides (link: shorturl.com/rw-aurigamesh-deck), proposed VPC checklist (note), example helm chart pointer (provided live)

Summary: quick technical sync to confirm hybrid listing requirements (marketplace connector, auth patterns), discuss quantization compatibility for customer models, and align on pilot scope and next steps.

Topics: marketplace listing requirements, VPC connector and SSO/SAML flow, KMS/HSM key handling, quantized model packaging and runtime compatibility, performance expectations for 8-bit/4-bit variants, observability/tracing hooks for model calls.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: alright hi everyone thanks for making time um quick roll call?
[00:07] Karla Singh: hey hi karla here
[00:09] Owen Park: owen here
[00:10] Lena Fritz: lena here
[00:12] David Ortiz: david, se on the redwood side
[00:14] Maya Chen: and ravi from product, cool. we'll do 45 ish minutes and leave time for Qs.

[00:30] Maya Chen: goal for today is to nail down the integration touchpoints for the marketplace listing and the hybrid/private deployment path — specifically VPC connector, SSO, and how your quantized models will be packaged for Redwood to run efficiently.

[01:05] Karla Singh: yes our PM asked for a clear checklist for listing and also any certs about encryption. we are SOC2 aligned but we can share docs, but curious about KMS flow for private customers.

[01:30] David Ortiz: sure, so for Redwood Private we support customer KMS via AWS KMS / GCP KMS / HSM integration, we can accept wrapped keys in the connector. small caveat is we need a service account with limited kms:Decrypt rights for the model runtime to pull keys during startup.

[01:58] Owen Park: can that be done without exposing keys to Redwood control plane? our security folks want key material kept customer-side for air-gapped use.

[02:15] Maya Chen: yes, for fully private on-prem or air-gapped we have an enclave mode where the runtime is customer-managed, and Redwood only ships the control plane metadata. in that mode keys never transit Redwood. for VPC-hosted private deployments we can do customer-managed KMS via key wrapping.

[02:42] Lena Fritz: ok that helps, do you have docs or a pattern?

[02:48] Maya Chen: we'll share the VPC connector checklist and a terraform snippet. David i'll note to attach the sample.

[03:10] David Ortiz: +1 — I'll include a sample IAM policy and the minimal ports we need open (gRPC, metrics, health).

[03:30] Karla Singh: great. second area — model packaging. we plan to ship our own quantized models (8-bit and some 4-bit experiments). we want to ensure runtime compatibility and also predictable latency.

[03:53] David Ortiz: okay quick note — Redwood runtime has optimized execution paths for 8-bit quantized weights across our kernels; 4-bit is trickier, requires a specific quantization schema and we currently validate two formats (q4_0 and q4_kxx) — we'll need a sample artifact to test.

[04:22] Owen Park: when you say 'artifact' do you mean a tar with tokenizer and model bin? our packaging is a helm chart plus a model image.

[04:30] David Ortiz: sample model artifact: model file(s), tokenizer config, a small manifest.json listing architecture, kv cache format expected and quantization metadata — that's the easiest. the helm chart is separate; for marketplace listing we just need a compatibility manifest.

[04:58] Karla Singh: right, we'll pull that together. question — any restrictions on the tokenizer? we use sentencepiece for most models.

[05:10] David Ortiz: sentencepiece is fine, just include vocab files and the tokenizer.json wrapper if you have one. sometimes transcription shows "K V cash" but that's fine — we can map.

[05:32] Lena Fritz: haha noted. next — listing UI asks for expected latency at 16k tokens — do you have guidance?

[05:45] Maya Chen: performance guidance: for hosted we publish percentile latencies by model family. For a dedicated/private pool with similar GPU class we estimate X ms per token for 8-bit and ~1.4X for 4-bit depending on kernel maturity. we can run a quick benchmark if you share a few prompts and token lengths.

[06:18] Owen Park: we'd want to run that ourselves too — can Redwood provide a small perf harness or script to run locally?

[06:26] David Ortiz: yes, we have a perf-runner script that hits the runtime endpoint and measures p50/p95. I'll share a docker image and runner in the repo.

[06:41] Karla Singh: excellent. security — SSO and marketplace auth: we use Okta and want SAML for admin flows, and token-based API keys for service-to-service. is that supported?

[06:55] Maya Chen: yep; marketplace listing uses SAML/SSO for the customer console and RBAC. API keys are scoped per-tenant and can be rotated via the console or API. For private deployments SAML connectors can be configured in the customer-managed control plane.

[07:18] Owen Park: what about audit logs and traceability? we need per-token tracing to link calls to user ids for audits.

[07:29] David Ortiz: we emit structured audit logs and allow log forwarding to your SIEM via syslog/CloudWatch/Stackdriver; for private we can forward into your logging cluster. trace IDs can propagate through the request headers, and we can add a custom header mapping if you need a specific claim.

[07:55] Lena Fritz: perfect. are there any marketplace gating items for compliance? sometimes the listing requires attestation.

[08:03] Maya Chen: typical: SOC2 summary, export control attestation, data residency info. we can provide a template. Karla, you mentioned SOC2 earlier — good to share.

[08:18] Karla Singh: yes we'll share the audit pack.

[08:24] David Ortiz: switching back to deployment patterns — caching & KV: many models benefit from prefix KV caching. curious how AurigaMesh uses caching patterns.

[08:36] Owen Park: we use per-session KV caching for chat contexts. we also have a separate short-term prefix cache for commonly used prompts (like policy prompts) to reduce token compute.

[08:50] David Ortiz: good — Redwood runtime supports prefix cache and can automatically serve cached token output for exact matches. for chat sessions we can pass a session id header so the runtime can manage session-level KV. small note: if you quantize aggressively the exact tokenization can shift and reduce cache hit rate, so we should test cache hit delta with your quantized artifacts.

[09:25] Karla Singh: aha ok that's important. so we'll include a short test set to estimate cache hit rate change after quantization.

[09:35] Maya Chen: yes please. we'll run baseline on full precision and then quantized. David will own that.

[09:44] David Ortiz: noted.

[10:05] [screen share] Ravi Patel: quick architecture sketch: for marketplace we'd have a connector image that customers can deploy in VPC; it handles auth, metrics and proxying, and registers runtime nodes with Redwood's control plane if customer opts in. otherwise full private mode the control plane is absent.

[10:35] Owen Park: in connector mode does it open inbound to our cluster or outbound?

[10:40] Ravi Patel: connector opens an outbound tunnel from your VPC to the Redwood ingress if using hosted control plane (TLS). for fully private it's all internal.

[10:58] Owen Park: good that fits our network constraints.

[11:10] Karla Singh: one of our legal folks asked about data retention for logs and prompts; do you store prompts at Redwood?

[11:20] Maya Chen: by default usage data is stored for analytics; we offer retention controls. for customers with strict retention we can configure zero retention for prompts and only keep minimal metadata. for enterprise we also support field-level redaction.

[11:46] Lena Fritz: can we redact before it leaves customer VPC?

[11:50] David Ortiz: yes you can run a pre-processing webhook in the connector that strips or hashes fields before sending. we'll add an example in the connector repo.

[12:10] Karla Singh: thanks. moving on — packaging details for 4-bit: our offline experiments show decent quality for a subset of models, but we need to know which quant schemas Redwood supports so we don't repackage wrong.

[12:26] David Ortiz: supported: q8 (8-bit symmetric), q4_0 and q4_kds (names approximate in transcript) — we'll put canonical names in the manifest doc. crucial is your manifest include the scaling factors per block and a sample inference script to reproduce logits ordering. sometimes tokenizer differences cause misalignment in outputs after quant.

[13:00] Owen Park: do you support fused kernels for Triton? we plan to run some workloads on Triton-based infra and also on bare metal.

[13:10] David Ortiz: we have Triton integrations for certain model families; for others we use our custom kernel stacks. If you plan Triton, we'll validate with your artifact but expect some perf delta.

[13:30] Karla Singh: ok what's a realistic SLA for a pilot? we want p95 latency under 1s for typical prompts under 2k tokens.

[13:40] Maya Chen: pilot SLA we can target p95 under 1s on a dedicated small GPU pool for 2k tokens using 8-bit quantized models, but results vary by model size and prompt complexity. let's scope sample prompts in the pilot.

[14:05] Lena Fritz: timeline: we need to be live in marketplace by end of Q2; is that feasible?

[14:12] Maya Chen: realistic — yes if pilot begins early April and packaging/testing takes 4–6 weeks. today we aim to finalize the checklist and sample artifacts then kickoff pilot.

[14:30] David Ortiz: I'll propose a pilot test matrix: functional compatibility, perf p50/p95 for three token lengths, cache hit delta, and security handshake validation.

[15:00] Karla Singh: sounds good. a few clarifying Qs from our infra engineer: what ports and protocols does the connector need?

[15:10] David Ortiz: primary outbound TCP port 443 (TLS), gRPC over HTTP2 for model calls, port 9090 for metrics (can be pulled), and health endpoints. we also support mutual TLS if you want mTLS between connector and runtime.

[15:34] Owen Park: how do we handle versioning for model updates? we want canary rollouts.

[15:40] Maya Chen: Redwood supports model version pinning and rollout policies (canary %, A/B). For marketplace listing we include recommended rollout policy and a default fallback model.

[16:03] Karla Singh: good. what about billing integration for marketplace? we want simple metering.

[16:10] Ravi Patel: marketplace metering can be token-based or seat-based. we'll share the listing doc; typically partners choose token-based with a per-1k token unit.

[16:30] Lena Fritz: we'll discuss pricing internally.

[16:40] [short pause]

[17:00] David Ortiz: quick note on observability hooks — we emit per-request traces and token-level cost estimates that show up in the console. for private we forward to your tracing stack. downside: tracking token-level costs requires sending token counts back to control plane unless you run purely private. we'll add an option for client-side aggregation.

[17:35] Owen Park: ok. another runtime question: memory footprint differences for 8-bit vs 4-bit?

[17:45] David Ortiz: roughly 8-bit halves memory vs 16-bit, 4-bit halves again but introduces more compute overhead for de-quant. expect more CPU/GPU cycles for 4-bit depending on kernel. we'll quantify in the perf report.

[18:10] Karla Singh: that'll help our capacity planning.

[18:22] Maya Chen: returning to next steps: we will share connector checklist, sample IAM policy, perf runner, and manifest template. AurigaMesh will share model artifacts + SOC2 summary + packaging README. then we'll schedule pilot scoping.

[18:40] Lena Fritz: noted. small ask: can Redwood include a short dev onboarding doc for our engineers?

[18:48] Maya Chen: yes we'll add a "developer quickstart" to the repo with example helm values.

[19:05] Karla Singh: perfect. any blockers we should call out now?

[19:10] Owen Park: only internal approvals and us bundling the quant artifacts; otherwise none.

[19:20] David Ortiz: i'll flag potential risk: 4-bit might require small changes to tokenizer or manifest. if you can ship a sample by early April, we can surface issues quickly.

[19:37] Maya Chen: awesome. last Qs?

[19:40] Lena Fritz: none from me.

[19:42] Karla Singh: none. thanks all.

[19:48] Maya Chen: recap: Redwood send VPC checklist, perf harness, IAM sample, manifest template. AurigaMesh send model artifact, SOC2 summary, packaging README. Pilot scoping call week of Apr 6. action items on deck.

[20:10] Owen Park: thanks everyone.
[20:12] David Ortiz: thanks, bye.

[52:00] [meeting end]

Notes: transcript contains occasional ASR mistakes (model names, quant flags), speaker labels approximate. Action items captured in metadata above.
